title: Pressure Simulation in Container
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js that simulates gas pressure inside a sealed container with a scoring system.

## Scene Setup
- Use a perspective camera at position (0, 3, 8) looking at origin.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.4) and a directional light at (5, 10, 5) with intensity 0.8.
- Background color: 0x1a1a2e.

## Container
- Create a transparent box (wireframe or semi-transparent faces) centered at origin, dimensions 4x4x4.
- Inside the container, spawn 20 small spheres (radius 0.15) representing gas particles. Color them 0x00ffcc. Place them at random positions within the container bounds.

## Physics Simulation
- Each particle has a velocity vector (random direction, magnitude ~0.02 initially).
- On each animation frame, move particles by their velocity.
- Implement wall collision: when a particle hits any wall of the container, reverse the appropriate velocity component. Each wall collision increments a global collision counter.
- Compute pressure as: pressure = (collisionCount / elapsed_seconds) / 6.0 (6 faces). Display this as a running average updated every second.

## Temperature Control
- Add an HTML button with id='heat-btn' labeled 'Heat (+50K)' that increases temperature.
- Add an HTML button with id='cool-btn' labeled 'Cool (-50K)' that decreases temperature.
- Initial temperature: 300K. Min: 100K, Max: 700K.
- When temperature changes, scale all particle speeds proportionally: new_speed = old_speed * sqrt(new_temp / old_temp).

## Scoring System
- Display a score on the HUD. The player earns 10 points each time they bring the pressure into a 'target zone'.
- On load, generate a random target pressure displayed on the HUD (between 5 and 25). When the measured pressure is within ±2 of the target for at least 2 consecutive seconds, award 10 points and generate a new random target.
- Display score with id='score-display'.

## Pause/Resume
- Add a button with id='pause-btn' labeled 'Pause'. Clicking toggles simulation pause. When paused, particles freeze and label changes to 'Resume'.

## HUD Elements
- A div with id='temp-display' showing current temperature like 'Temperature: 300 K'.
- A div with id='pressure-display' showing 'Pressure: XX.X'.
- A div with id='target-display' showing 'Target: XX.X'.
- A div with id='score-display' showing 'Score: 0'.
- A div with id='particle-count' showing 'Particles: 20'.
- Style HUD in top-left corner, white text on semi-transparent dark background.

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- temperature (number, current temp in K)
- pressure (number, current computed pressure)
- targetPressure (number, current target)
- score (number, current score)
- particleCount (number, always 20)
- paused (boolean)
- collisionCount (number, total wall collisions)
- elapsedTime (number, seconds since start, not counting paused time)
- particleSpeedAvg (number, average speed magnitude of all particles)

Update __3D_STATE__ every frame.
physics_constraints: Particles must bounce elastically off container walls. Speed scales with sqrt(temperature). Pressure is proportional to collision rate. No particles may escape the container bounds [-2, 2] in each axis. No NaN values in any state field.
